analysis.title: Pilot performance indicators against their targets
analysis.method: Pilot start 2026-10-01; 1.5 of 5 enrolment months elapsed.

rows: Pre-screening compliance (given SLDP after a passed screen)
Consenting (enrolled patients who consented at Day 0)

analysis.finding: 2 of 8 indicators met or on track. Not met or behind: Serious adverse event rate (CEM participants); CEM enrolment: Day 0 completed; CEM enrolment: Day 3 FBC done.

analysis.title: Incidence of adverse events after SLDP (CEM cohort)
analysis.method: 302 participants followed for 4,147 person-days (median 14 days each). Exact binomial and Poisson confidence intervals.

rows: Signs of haemolysis (dark urine, jaundice or Hb drop)

analysis.finding: 19.5% of participants (95% CI 15.2 to 24.5) reported at least one adverse event; 4 serious event(s) and 0 death(s) so far.

analysis.title: Adverse events by sign or symptom
analysis.finding: Most frequent: Headache, Nausea, Dizziness. Signs of haemolysis (dark urine, jaundice, Hb drop) are tracked separately in Objective 2.

analysis.title: Time to first adverse event (Kaplan-Meier)
analysis.finding: By Day 3, 11.8% of participants had a first adverse event; by Day 28, 27.1%. Most events start early, in line with the primaquine exposure window.

chart.label: Cumulative probability of a first AE (%)

analysis.title: Change in haemoglobin from Day 0 to Day 3
analysis.method: 263 participants with Hb measured on Day 0 and Day 3.

rows: Fall of 2 g/dL or more (95% CI)
Fall of 3 g/dL or more (95% CI)

analysis.finding: Hb changed by a mean of -0.49 g/dL (95% CI -0.58 to -0.40; paired t-test p < 0.001). 6 participant(s) (2.3%) had a fall of 2 g/dL or more, the protocol safety threshold.

analysis.title: What predicts the change in Hb? (linear regression)
analysis.finding: Associated with the size of the Hb change at the 5% level: G6PD deficient (vs normal/unknown).

analysis.title: Adverse events and Hb fall by subgroup
analysis.method: 302 CEM participants followed. Protocol subgroups: children (under 5, 5-14), anaemic at baseline, possible G6PD deficiency.
analysis.finding: AE frequency differs significantly (p < 0.05) by: Sex. Check the intervals before acting: early numbers are small.

analysis.title: Children under 5 compared with older participants

rows: Hb fall of 2 g/dL or more

analysis.finding: Children under 5 get the smallest primaquine doses and are a protocol priority subgroup; a risk ratio clearly above 1 would need review by the safety team.

analysis.title: Risk factors for any adverse event (logistic regression)
analysis.finding: Independently associated with an AE (p < 0.05): Male (vs female).

analysis.title: Risk factors for a fall in Hb of 2 g/dL or more (logistic regression)
analysis.method: 263 participants, 6 with a fall of 2 g/dL or more.
analysis.finding: Independently associated with a fall of 2 g/dL or more (p < 0.05): G6PD deficient (vs normal/unknown).

analysis.title: Time to first AE by age group (Cox regression)
analysis.method: 302 participants, 59 events. Proportional hazards test (global) p = 0.686.
analysis.finding: Hazard ratios above 1 mean an earlier and more frequent first AE than the reference group.

analysis.title: Signal check: signs reported more often when primaquine is suspected
analysis.finding: No sign meets the signal criteria so far.

analysis.title: Retention in CEM follow-up (Kaplan-Meier)
analysis.finding: Estimated retention to Day 28: 95.9%. The protocol defines loss to follow-up as 2 unsuccessful scheduled follow-ups.

analysis.title: Reporting timeliness against the FDA deadlines
analysis.method: 81 events with an onset and a report date.
analysis.finding: 80 of 81 events (99%) were reported within the deadline.

analysis.title: Day 3 parasitology (repeat test)
analysis.method: Among Day 3 visits where the test was repeated.
analysis.finding: Positivity on Day 3 reflects ACT response; persistent positivity should be followed up clinically.
